faq_discord_scopes_title: Why is Discord asking for so many scary permissions?
faq_discord_scopes_p1: Unfortunately Discord has discontinued their activities.write scope for applications.
faq_discord_scopes_p2: This means the only way to write activities is via the Social SDK. This SDK is designed so Discord can be implemented into games, which is why it needs so many scopes.

faq_tokens_title: How are my Nintendo tokens stored? Can you see them?
faq_tokens_p1: Your sign-in details, the Nintendo session token and Switch Online access tokens Reef uses to fetch your presence and friends, plus the webview cookies for game services, are all encrypted before they are saved, those values only ever live in the database as ciphertext.
faq_tokens_p2: Encryption keys are kept confidential, are never logged, and are not stored in the database or its backups, so a stolen database copy is useless on its own. Stored data is also tamper-evident: if any of it is altered or forged, Reef refuses to decrypt it.
faq_tokens_p3: Tokens are only decrypted for a split second, in memory, when Reef needs to talk to Nintendo on your behalf. Nothing is ever written back in plaintext, and the app has no admin view, API or export that can display your tokens.
faq_tokens_p4: Your Nintendo Account ID is stored in the clear, but that is a public identifier, not a secret. Tokens are only ever sent to Nintendo’s servers (and to nxapi-znca-api, the service that decrypts and re-encrypts Nintendo Switch App requests, see the link above). Deleting your account (Settings -> Delete account) removes all of it.
faq_ban_p1: Most likely not. Nobody has been banned yet for legitimately using third-party clients (including nxapi).
faq_ban_p2: However, a small subset of users was banned from SplatNet 3 in 2023 for attempting to exploit elements of SplatNet 3. This only resulted in a ban from SplatNet 3, no other Nintendo services were affected, including their accounts or consoles.
